title: The Qur’an, Isra and Mi‘raj
intro: The night journey to Jerusalem and the rising through the seven heavens – where Salah was given to us.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Glory be to the One who took His servant by night from Al-Masjid al-Haram to Al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed, to show him some of Our signs. Truly, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing. <small>(Qur’an, Al-Isra 17:1, meaning)</small>

The Qur’an tells us about the Isra and Mi‘raj – a miracle Allah gave to Muhammad (SAW). It was Allah’s gift and reward to him after ten years of hard work as a Prophet and all the troubles he had faced.

learn.title: The Year of Sorrow
learn.html: The Quraysh tried to turn Muhammad (SAW) away from his mission. They offered him wealth, wives and power, but he wanted none of it – his only wish was to fulfil his mission. When they saw he would not give up, they put even more pressure on the Muslims and him. In that time his wife Khadijah and his uncle Abu Talib died, so that year is called the Year of Sorrow (‘Am al-Huzn). It was the hardest time for the Prophet (SAW) and the Muslims.

Isra and Mi‘raj happened on the 27th of Rajab, in the 11th year of prophethood, in 621. The Isra is the first part: the night journey from Al-Masjid al-Haram in Makkah to Al-Masjid al-Aqsa in Al-Quds (Jerusalem). There the Prophet (SAW), as imam, led two rak‘ahs of prayer with the souls of the earlier prophets.

learn.text: Mi‘raj – rising through the seven heavens

learn.html: All of them welcomed him, honoured him and accepted his prophethood. Then he was raised to Sidrat al-Muntaha and Qaba Qawsayn – where no angel had ever reached. During the Mi‘raj he saw Jannah, Jahannam and many signs that others could not see. He was in a special, highest place before Allah, and there Salah was made a duty for Muslims.

learn.title: The next morning
learn.html: The next day the Prophet (SAW) told the people of Makkah about his journey. They asked him to describe Al-Masjid al-Aqsa and Jerusalem, and he described every detail. Even though they knew he had never been there, the mushrikun did not believe that the Isra and Mi‘raj had happened.

learn.text: Salah – the mi‘raj of the believer

learn.html: Salah was given on the Mi‘raj – this shows how important Salah is in a Muslim’s life. Salah brings beautiful feelings, peace and strength. It lights up the heart, cleans the soul and keeps us away from everything bad. A Muslim is closest to Allah in Salah, especially in sajdah. Muhammad (SAW) said: “A person is closest to Allah while in sajdah.” (Muslim)

When we pray five times a day, we stand before our Lord and speak to Him, close to Him, without anyone in between. That is why Salah is called the mi‘raj of the believer. A true Muslim does not see Salah as a burden, but waits for it with longing.

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: Isra = Makkah → Jerusalem. Mi‘raj = through the seven heavens. Its gift is Salah.

practice.title: The seven heavens
practice.prompt: Put the prophets in the order of the heavens where Muhammad (SAW) met them, from the 1st to the 7th.

Arriving at Al-Masjid al-Aqsa in Jerusalem
Leading the prophets in two rak‘ahs
Telling the people of Makkah the next day

practice.title: Talk with your muallim
prompts: 💬 The Qur’an, Isra and Mi‘raj – how are they connected? What did they mean for the Prophet (SAW), and what do they mean for us today?
🕌 Do you wait for Salah with longing, or does it feel like a burden? How can it feel more like a mi‘raj?
